title: Recall-context identification from glial calcium

titles: Hippocampal astrocytic calcium sequences during learning and memory recall

scientific_question: Can astrocytic calcium distinguish recall contexts across animals without context-coded filenames?
primary_outputs: Context probabilities for equal-duration neural windows.

data_manifest.file_count_scope: Top-level published assets, including code/docs where packaged together; not a participant count.

recording_contract.neural: Per-animal collection objects contain accepted_traces and Timestamps; the release also includes accepted-trace CSVs and original Cell_Traces CSVs. These are astrocytic/glial calcium measurements, not neuronal spikes.
recording_contract.labels: Habituation, fear conditioning, context A and context B sessions; per-mouse event_times_cxta/cxtb, freezing vectors and Anymaze behavior. Context is an experimental label; event definitions must be fixed before scientific scoring.
recording_contract.time_alignment: Figure3 reads Timestamps[:traces.shape[0]] and per-animal event times, with event-aligned odd/even analyses. Context and behavior exports provide matching animal/session filenames. Units/monotonicity and trace-event range checks remain execution gates.
recording_contract.biological_ids: archive README names astroF*/astroM* animals and hab/fc/cxta/cxtb sessions. Inspected Figure3 explicitly selects astroF3,F5,F6,F7,F9,F10,M3,M4,M5,M9,M10 (11 mice) for a particular analysis; this is not claimed to be the full archive cohort.
recording_contract.evidence: Four real-input ZIP directories, published checksums, author upstream-loading README and Figure3 source inspected. Exact collection, trace and event filenames are present; no data objects or traces loaded.
